articles.author: Gaming News
articles.description:
Splitgate 2, the hotly anticipated follow-up to 2021’s surprise hit, is hitting pause just weeks after its June launch—“unlaunching” back to open beta. 1047 Games admits it launched too early, so it’s shelving its roadmap, cutting an undisclosed number of staff, and even shutting down original Splitgate servers to trim costs. CEO Ian Proulx says the team will overhaul everything from expensive cosmetics (goodbye $80 skin bundles) to core features like ranked modes, more portal walls and mode-specific playlists, this time working hand-in-glove with the community before a planned early 2026 rerelease.
Despite the reset, Season 3 updates, bug fixes and special events will keep players hooked, but 95% of the studio’s efforts are going toward the big relaunch. Layoffs are already underway (details under wraps), and while the OG servers go dark next month, peer-to-peer or offline play might fill the gap. Proulx even owned up to the missteps—and that infamous “Make FPS Great Again” hat—vowing to learn from mistakes and grind toward a truly polished comeback.
articles.title: Splitgate 2 ‘unlaunches,' studio to cut staff ahead of 2026 rerelease

articles.author: Gaming News
articles.description:

He capped it off with an appropriately cryptic, hopeful message: “Even if you don’t notice, someone is connected to you, watching over you” as a reminder that there’s always someone out there willing to protect you.
articles.title: A month on, Hideo Kojima says 79% of Death Stranding 2 players continued after credits rolled

articles.author: AI News
articles.description:
Trump’s new AI action plan promises “bias-free” models for federal use—but the fine print reveals it wants AI to toe his line on “truth,” axing any talk of climate change, DEI or “misinformation.” Under the guise of protecting free speech, the order pressures developers to ditch “woke Marxist lunacy” and adopt the White House’s version of reality.  
It’s a classic bait-and-switch: an anti-bias mandate that actually codifies top-down ideological bias through procurement power. Big AI players like Google, OpenAI and Anthropic have mostly shrugged, lured by the plan’s pro-industry goodies—despite potential First Amendment fights over whether the feds can punish models for daring to mention climate science or call out racial bias.
articles.title: Trump's Anti-Bias AI Order Is Just More Bias

articles.author: AI News
articles.description:
The Trump administration’s new “Doge AI Deregulation Decision Tool” is set to trawl through some 200,000 federal regulations and flag half of them for deletion by the first anniversary of his second inauguration. Internal PowerPoints show HUD has already used it to review 1,083 regulatory sections and the CFPB leaned on AI for “100% of deregulations,” all part of Trump’s promise to unleash the “most aggressive regulatory reduction” ever.
White House flack Harrison Fields insists the project’s in its “early stages” and no final plan’s been green-lit, while praising Doge’s “best and brightest.” The office—once helmed by Elon Musk—includes newbies like 19-year-old Edward “Big Balls” Coristine, raising eyebrows about how AI will reshape the federal rulebook.
articles.title: Doge reportedly using AI tool to create ‘delete list' of federal regulations

Eddie Murphy has announced on TODAY that he’ll don the trench coat and magnifying glass as the new Inspector Clouseau in an upcoming Pink Panther reboot. In the same chat with Al Roker, he teased other projects on deck—playing funk legend George Clinton, jumping back into Shrek 5 and, yes, leading the classic bumbling detective franchise.
Murphy winked that his Clouseau “has to be French, but he could also be Haitian… he’s Black, for sure,” putting his own spin on the role first made famous by Peter Sellers and later revived by Steve Martin. At 64, the comedy icon says he’s shifted from wise-cracking upstart to “the old voice of reason”—and admits action scenes take a bit more out of him these days.
